sections.html:
Henderson sits on a bluff above the Ohio River in north-central Henderson County, about 10 miles south of Evansville, Indiana, and 30 miles west of Owensboro. The July 2025 estimate is 27,822 residents, a little under the 2020 figure of 27,981. The slow dip means most buyers are local households or people who commute across the river.

As county seat, Henderson funnels deeds, tax bills and court filings through the same few downtown blocks. A house with clean title and no open city orders closes quickly. An estate still in probate, an unpaid weed lien or a back tax bill drags things out, so clear those first.

The middle of the owner-occupied range is $160,100. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $1,253 a month on housing, owners without one spend $494, and renters pay a median $771. Only 54.1% of households own, so rentals are a big slice of the housing stock. There are 12,341 households, averaging 2.18 people, and median household income is $48,186.

Adults 65 and older are 18.8% of residents, a group that often ends up selling an inherited or long-held home. At these price points, repair bills weigh heavily on the final number. A roof and furnace job can swallow a large share of the sale price, so owners with deferred maintenance often compare an as-is sale with paying contractors first. Gather two or three quotes before you decide.

Henderson began as a river landing called Red Banks and was laid out in 1797 with unusually wide streets. Dark tobacco drove the economy for generations. Older residential areas such as Audubon, Weaverton and the former East End grew up around that industry, and many houses there date from the early 1900s. Expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at wiring, plumbing and foundations in a house that age.

The climate is humid and warm, so inspectors also check roof age, attic airflow and cooling equipment. Write down the age of each system before the first showing.

US 41 crosses the Bi-State Vietnam Gold Star Bridges to Evansville and runs south toward Madisonville and Hopkinsville. I-69 in Kentucky ends at the US 41 and US 60 interchange at Henderson. Local industry includes aluminum, automotive and appliance parts, plastic injection molding, tool and die work and food processing. Buyers with jobs at those plants or in Evansville tend to shop within a short drive of US 41.

sections.h2: Who to call before listing or closing
sections.html:
Four offices touch most sales.

Henderson offices that touch a sale
OfficeWhat it handlesContact detail
City Code EnforcementBuilding codes, property maintenance, signs, zoning questions100 Fifth Street, (270) 831-1277, weekdays 8:00 to 5:00
Board of Zoning AdjustmentVariances, conditional use permits, appeals of zoning decisionsMeets the second Wednesday monthly except January
Henderson County SheriffCurrent real estate tax billsBills mailed late October or early November, payable from November 1
Henderson County ClerkRecording deeds, delinquent tax bills, lien releases20 N Main Street, second floor, (270) 827-5753

Ask Code Enforcement whether any order is open on your address before you sign a contract. The buyer's closing agent will search for one.

Since July 1, 2017, a Code Enforcement Board has handled property maintenance and nuisance cases. Final orders are posted by the city, and registered lienholders get a monthly email notice. Typical entries are weeds, rubbish, clutter and inoperable vehicles.

  • A final order can be appealed within 30 days of issue under KRS 65.8831.
  • A lienholder of record has 45 days from the emailed notice to fix the violation or pay the fines and abatement charges.
  • If no one acts, the city's lien ranks ahead of earlier liens, though tax liens for the state, county, schools and city still come first (KRS 65.8835).

Charges like these are normally paid from the sale money, so the totals must be known before closing day. Phone (270) 831-1277 and request the file on your parcel.

sections.h2: Property tax and deed tax at closing
sections.html:
Real estate bills come from the Sheriff's Office in late October or early November and are payable starting November 1. A bill still open on the January 1 after its due date is delinquent. The Sheriff then passes it to the County Clerk, where interest runs at 1% a month on top of penalties, and the property stays encumbered until the bill is paid in full.

The person giving the deed pays a state deed tax of 50 cents per $500 of declared value, rounded up (KRS 142.050). The clerk collects it at the counter before the deed is recorded. Foreclosure sales and voluntary surrenders in place of foreclosure fall outside the tax, as do gifts between parent and child for nominal money.

The closing statement usually bills the seller for the months of the tax year already owned. Ask the Sheriff's Office for a current figure so the statement matches the bill.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or short-term rental
sections.html:
Yes, you can sell one, though zoning limits what a buyer may do with it. Land use is set in Appendix A of the city's Code of Ordinances, and Code Enforcement explains setbacks, allowed uses and parking. In April 2024 the Board of Commissioners took up an ordinance amending that appendix for short-term rental property, which touches several residential, business and riverfront districts. Check with Code Enforcement on your parcel before you advertise the house as a short-term rental.

When tenants occupy the house, collect the lease and the deposit ledger early, since buyers ask when the term ends.

After a contract is signed, the closing agent searches title at the County Clerk's office. Open tax bills, code liens and any mortgage show up in that search, and each is paid from your proceeds. That is why a payoff letter from the lender, a tax figure from the Sheriff and a code file from the city are worth requesting before you list.

A cash purchase skips the appraisal and lender review, so the closing day is set by agreement. A conventional sale adds showings, an appraisal and loan approval. Either way, you sign the deed, pay the deed tax at the clerk's counter, and the deed is recorded.

• List with an agent. Suits a sound house on a street buyers recognize, though showings and mortgage approval stretch the calendar.
  • Take a cash offer. The buyer takes the house in its present state, with no repair negotiation, appraisal or lender review.
  • Clear the obstacle first. Paying off a small weed lien or finishing probate can reopen the regular market.

Compare what you keep from each route after deed tax, prorated taxes, liens and repairs.

faqs.q: How fast can a house sell in Henderson, KY?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. A cash purchase closes on an agreed date, and a conventional sale adds showings, an appraisal and loan approval. Either way the deed is recorded at the Henderson County Clerk, after open code orders and tax bills are paid off.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed transfer tax in Henderson County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it, since the tax falls on the grantor named in the deed. KRS 142.050 sets the rate at $0.50 per $500, and the clerk collects before recording. Foreclosure transfers are exempt.

faqs.q: What if I owe back property tax on my Henderson house?
faqs.a: Pay them off at or before closing. Bills left unpaid past January 1 move to the County Clerk and grow by 1% a month plus penalties, and the property stays under a lien. The Clerk's Office at 20 N Main Street can quote a payoff.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Henderson house with open Code Enforcement violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid fines and abatement costs can become a city lien that outranks earlier private liens but not tax liens, and the total is paid from the sale money. Phone Code Enforcement at (270) 831-1277 for the file before pricing the house.

faqs.q: Do I need to make repairs before selling a Henderson home?
faqs.a: No. A buyer who purchases the house unrepaired takes the work on, while a retail buyer may ask for fixes after inspection. Collect contractor quotes before choosing, since a big repair bill takes a large share of a price near $160,100.
